$comment: The front-desk speed measurement, RECORDED AS ABSENT. H-MIG-10.
The requirement is a walk-in bookable in under 10,000 ms at the 95th percentile on the seeded
dataset. This file holds no figure, and that is the measurement rather than a gap: a wall-clock
percentile taken in an agent container with several agents on four cores is a figure about the
container, and written here it would be indistinguishable from a figure about the product
(docs/CONTRIBUTING-AGENT-BRIEF.md rule 23). This unit's own manifest note says it in fewer words:
real-device results recorded as absent, not assumed passing.
`verdict` is `not_measured`, which is a VALUE and not an absence, and `p95Ms` is null rather than 0:
a zero would pass a ten-second budget with room to spare, and an absent field would read exactly
like a report nobody had got round to generating (ADR 0070, applied to a latency instead of a cost).
HOW TO TAKE IT. On the machine the claim is about:
WALK_IN_SPEED_MEASURE=1 pnpm exec vitest run -c vitest.integration.config.ts \
The suite prints the percentile, the sample count and the budget on stderr; write them here with the
machine, and `apps/web/e2e/walk-in-speed.itest.ts` will hold this file to the verdict the arithmetic
gives for its own figures — so a hand-edited `within_budget` over three samples fails.
`minimumSamples` is 20 because that is the smallest count at which a 95th percentile is not simply
the slowest observation; a report with fewer is `not_measured` rather than optimistic.
